title: Client-Centered Therapy in its Context of Research
coreMove: Subject a humane practice to inquiry without turning the client into a research object.
sourcePressure: Client-centered therapy is placed inside research without letting empirical context erase the human core of the approach. No split source sidecar exists for ch12; frozen TOC and book skeleton support the heading, part placement, and broad intent only, with no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Assuming research either proves the whole practice or betrays it.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of client-centered therapy
counterintuition: Most people think X, but Y
It is not about being nice
The paradox is that acceptance changes everything
